usageNotes: Use this to enable, disable, or tune the per-container firewall (default policies, logging levels, DHCP/NDP/MAC filter toggles) for a specific LXC container. The firewall must also be enabled at the cluster and node level for per-container rules to take effect; setting 'enable: true' here alone is not sufficient. Returns null synchronously — no UPID is issued.

examples.summary: Enable the container firewall with DROP default policies and warning-level logging

tips: Use 'digest' (from the GET options response) to prevent race conditions when multiple administrators may be editing firewall config simultaneously.
The 'delete' param accepts a comma-separated list of option names (e.g. 'log_level_in,radv') to revert specific fields to their defaults without touching others.
ipfilter is particularly useful for containers: it automatically restricts each interface to only its configured IP(s), blocking IP spoofing at the hypervisor level.
macfilter defaults to enabled (1); disabling it allows a container to send traffic from arbitrary MAC addresses, which is a security risk on shared networks.
radv (Router Advertisement) should only be enabled on containers acting as IPv6 routers/gateways — enabling it on a normal workload container can disrupt IPv6 on the segment.
